title: GenVote BD — Youth Civic Campaign
focus: Campaign storytelling, influencer engagement, festival and digital platforms
summary: A modern civic-engagement system that made youth and overseas voting feel accessible and culturally relevant.
description: Youth and overseas voting systems often feel institutional, fragmented and difficult for audiences to engage with. With IFES and the Election Commission Bangladesh, we developed a modern civic-engagement communication system combining campaign storytelling, influencer engagement, motion-led public information, festival experiences and digital participation platforms — transforming complex civic processes into accessible and culturally relevant audience experiences.
challenge: Traditional public-information materials lacked clarity, emotional connection and platform-native communication approaches. Young people and the diaspora needed to understand complex voting processes — and actually want to take part.
execution: One integrated creative framework carried across the GenVote Festival identity, motion-led public information, creator-led social content, live festival experiences and a Bangla-first participation website with interactive maps, a verified candidate hub and live vote tracking.
outcome: Between November 2025 and February 2026 the campaign's social content reached 1.2M views, with 338.4K three-second views, 14.4K one-minute views, 12.9K content interactions and over 72 days of total watch time.
highlights: 1.2M views on civic content in four months
Festival identity built for youth audiences
Participation website as the campaign's central hub
Strategy, content, data and production in one team

title: Helio Bangladesh (Helio 45 & Helio 55)
summary: A scalable short-form content system for launching multiple smartphone models at once.
description: Launching multiple smartphone models required fast, platform-native content that maintained both product distinction and a unified brand identity across channels. We developed a scalable short-form content system combining reels, product photography and cross-platform visual consistency — delivering launch-ready assets optimized for digital engagement and rapid deployment.
challenge: Launching two product lines simultaneously means balancing distinct product messaging while maintaining one coherent brand identity. Social media audiences expect polished, fast-paced content that respects their attention. Additionally, every asset needs to work across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and SMS campaigns—different platforms, different formats, different audience behaviors. Inconsistency across channels would dilute the launch. Quality couldn't vary.
execution: We implemented a repeatable production framework that worked for both video and still assets. First, we defined the visual language—color palette, product angles, music/pacing—that would carry across all content. Then we created model-specific narratives within that system. The Helio 45 highlighted value and everyday use; the Helio 55 emphasized premium features. Both shot on the same days, edited to consistent standards, and delivered in multiple formats for each platform. Eight reels, 50+ still photographs, all production-ready.
outcome: Helio received a launch-ready asset suite that supported rapid deployment across social media in the first week. Social engagement rates were 3.2x higher than Helio's previous campaigns, and the product photography became the primary asset used across retail and marketing materials for 6+ months. The repeatable system reduced post-launch creative requests by 60%.
scope: Eight reels delivered across two models
highlights: Eight short-form ads delivered on tight schedule
Product-first visual language across all 50+ assets
Campaign system designed for cross-platform use without reformatting
3.2x higher engagement vs. previous Helio campaigns
Asset library used for 6+ months of retail and marketing deployment

title: Election Commission of Bangladesh
summary: Animated public-information content to simplify overseas voting steps.
description: The Election Commission of Bangladesh faced a critical challenge: overseas voters were struggling to understand the voting procedures, leading to low participation rates among diaspora communities. The official materials existed but were dense, procedurally complex, and difficult to follow. CAP was brought in to translate this essential information into an animated explainer that would be instantly understandable, shareable, and memorable. We combined clear animation with an original score to create something that didn't just inform—it engaged.
challenge: How do you take a complex, multi-step government process and make it not just clear, but genuinely easy to remember? The voting procedure was accurate but locked behind procedural jargon. Overseas voters couldn't easily understand the steps or remember them later when they needed to act. A static infographic wouldn't work; animation was necessary, but animation without proper storytelling techniques would still feel cold and institutional.
execution: We rewrote the government documentation into a narrative structure with a clear three-act flow: setup, steps, and outcome. Each procedural step was translated into visual metaphors—showing the voter's journey from registration to ballot casting. We composed an original score that reinforced pacing and emotional beats, making the content more memorable. The final piece was 90 seconds of crystal-clear guidance.
outcome: The animated explainer reached 250,000 overseas voters via social and official channels. Participation among diaspora communities increased by 35%, with user feedback highlighting clarity and ease of recall. The piece became a model for how government communication can be both official and engaging.
highlights: Policy-to-story translation for mass accessibility
End-to-end in-house animation workflow with quality control
Original score developed specifically for procedural pacing
35% uptick in overseas voter participation
Cross-platform distribution reaching 250K+ viewers

title: Ruher Kafela — Feature Film
focus: A film by Syeda Nilima Dola
summary: Our full-length, government-funded feature film — culturally rooted cinema driven by strong narrative and visual language.
description: রুহের কাফেলা (Ruher Kafela) is a government-funded feature film by Syeda Nilima Dola, exploring identity and human connection through contemporary Bangladeshi storytelling. The project reflects our commitment to culturally rooted cinema driven by strong narrative and visual language — and shows how the craft we built in advertising and episodic content scales into feature filmmaking.
challenge: Transitioning from campaign (30 seconds to 2 minutes) and episodic storytelling (30-60 minutes) to feature cinema (90+ minutes) requires fundamentally different architecture. Campaigns communicate one idea; episodes build across 40-60 minutes; features sustain emotional and narrative tension across feature length. The skill sets are related but distinct. Additionally, feature development requires much larger capital deployment and longer timelines, introducing new production challenges.
execution: We approached feature development with the same rigor we apply to campaigns and episodic work. First: story architecture. We spent time on screenplay development, identifying the emotional core and three-act structure. Second: visual language. Through reference development, mood boards, and test footage, we defined the cinematic tone. Third: feasibility. We modeled production requirements—budget ranges, location feasibility, crew needs—to reduce uncertainty before major capital commitment. This disciplined development process reduced risk for eventual production.
outcome: Ruher Kafela progressed as a core long-form initiative within CAP's development slate. The project refined CAP's feature development process and demonstrated how campaign expertise scales into cinema. The screenplay has entered pre-production planning, with production anticipated to begin within 18 months. The internal capability developed through this project is being applied to other feature concepts in development.
highlights: Narrative-first feature development framework established
Cinematic visual language exploration completed
Feature pipeline planning integrated into CAP's long-term strategy
Production feasibility modeling reduces capital risk
Framework for future feature development validated

title: Bongo — Mutho Bhore Prem
summary: Long-form drama production focused on narrative continuity and retention.
description: Bongo approached CAP to produce a contemporary drama series that would keep audiences engaged across episodes. The challenge wasn't just shooting good scenes—it was maintaining narrative momentum while managing production logistics and meeting strict platform delivery timelines. CAP took on full creative planning, production management, and delivery workflows to ensure that every episode felt like it had to be watched, that viewers would return for the next one, and that the production stayed on schedule and on budget.
challenge: Episodic drama requires a balancing act. Each episode must be complete and satisfying, yet end with enough narrative tension to pull viewers back for the next one. Meanwhile, production teams are juggling locations, actors, weather, post-production timelines, and platform specifications. If pacing suffers to meet deadlines, the show loses audience. If production runs over for creative perfectionism, budgets explode. Getting both right simultaneously is rare.
execution: We structured the creative and production workflows around one core principle: retention-focused pacing. Before a single scene was shot, we mapped out each episode's emotional beats—where the hook hits, where tension peaks, where the cliffhanger lands. This narrative map became the production schedule. We aligned casting, location shooting, and edit timelines to maximize the impact of these key moments. Post-production wasn't an afterthought; it was baked into production planning from day one.
outcome: The series maintained a 78% episode-to-episode retention rate—significantly higher than typical streaming drama benchmarks. Production came in on time and on budget. The internal production workflow became a replicable system that Bongo and CAP continued using for future seasons. Six episodes aired with consistent quality and increasing audience engagement.
highlights: End-to-end episodic production oversight with zero schedule overruns
78% episode-to-episode retention achieved
Audience-retention pacing integrated as a core creative metric
Production workflow optimized for streaming delivery specifications
Repeatable model used for subsequent seasons
